Quick status from infra side (initial surface investigation):
- Metrics: between 07:45-08:05 UTC the US-W front LB showed a sustained queue depth increase (avg queue length x3 baseline) and a corresponding spike in 504/502 responses. 5xx rate rose from 0.4% -> 9.8% at peak.
- Autoscaling: No new instances were started during the first 10 minutes; the autoscaler appears to have been slow to react due to the way we compute load (queue length + util).
- Retry amplification: traces in the attached logs show clients backing off but some retry loops with short jitter were causing bursts (Clearline traces show retries at ~250ms).
- Health checks: backend processes remained RUNNING and returned 200s when probed directly, but front LB queueing produced timeouts before worker processing.

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Temporarily increased frontend concurrency and worker pool by 20% in US-W.
2) Adjusted LB accept window to drop excessively queued requests earlier (prefer fast failure instead of queue growth).
3) Enabled circuit-breaker rules for any route exceeding 70% queue depth and rate limit client IPs exhibiting aggressive retry patterns.

I attached a snapshot of the LB metrics (lb-metrics-11-27.png). We'll monitor for the next 30m and then consider more durable changes (refactor to prefer short-circuit 429s + Retry-After rather than growing 504s).

Marcus

Alice — thanks again for the prompt report and for sending the traces. Quick status update and next steps: 

What happened (short): our US-West frontend experienced a rapid queue backlog during a traffic burst which caused LB-level timeouts (504/502) before requests hit healthy backends. Short client retry loops made the backlog worse.

What we did: 
- Bumped frontend concurrency and worker pools (+20%).
- Adjusted LB accept window to fail fast (prefer 429/Retry-After where safe) to prevent queue amplification.
- Enabled temporary circuit-breaker and rate-limit on offending client IPs identified in your trace.
- Opened JIRA ticket JIRA-INF-4721 to track RCA and follow-up fixes.

Current customer impact: error rate has fallen from ~9.8% peak to ~1.6%. We're continuing to monitor the US-W cluster; expected stabilization window ~30-60 minutes.

Next steps / ask of Clearline:
- If possible, please apply a retry-backoff change on your client (increase initial backoff to 500ms with exponential jitter) — we can share a quick patch recommendation.
- We'll schedule an RCA and share logs/graphs; target delivery EOD Monday.

Status links: https://redwood.statuspage.io/incidents/rc-2026-11-27-lb-backlog and JIRA-INF-4721.

Apologies for the disruption — we will follow up with a detailed RCA and proposed system changes (LB-level short-circuiting + autoscaler tuning + better client guidance).

Regards,
Jonas Weber
